_comment: Entry rule (a) of the chapter: cohorts must be free of the disease under study when assembled.

stem.en: The plant's 1970 personnel records show that three of the tank cleaners already had the liver tumour when the cohort follow-up opens. What do the cohort's rules say about these three?

text.en: They are excluded from both cohorts, because a cohort must be free of the disease under study when it begins
They stay in the study cohort, because their tumours make the outcome likelier to appear
They move to the control cohort, since their tank-cleaning days ended when they fell ill
They are kept, and their follow-up is counted from the date the tumour was diagnosed

explanation.en: The chapter's first condition on assembling cohorts is that they must be free from the disease under study: members are examined against the records, and anyone who already shows the disease is excluded. A man who already has the tumour is not a person at risk of developing it, so keeping him would inflate the cohort's case count with outcomes that pre-date the follow-up. The same rule is what your exercise demanded before any file could enter a bin.

hints.en: The cohort measures new disease during follow-up. What does a man who arrived already ill do to that measure?
